first_impression: Pretty deck, Apple-silicon-only. Metal kernel per robot is real engineering, but 2D walker and MuJoCo CPU baseline are carefully chosen.
confusing: Slide 6 'days of practice' is simulated robot time, a vanity metric that sounds like wall-clock work
Slide 10 headline 40x vs 22x at the 4,096 actually trained; two numbers and a 121x chain compete
Slide 2 leans on one JAX maintainer quote instead of surveying MLX/Taichi/Genesis Metal backends
doubts: 40x is vs MuJoCo C rollout on CPU with 3D general contacts; planar impulse-only physics is not apples to apples
No MJX/Warp/Genesis/Taichi-Metal comparison; 'no fast GPU path on a Mac' is asserted, not shown
Training is 72% PPO update, so the kernel speedup barely changes the real time to a policy
Metal kernel claim: want to see kernel occupancy, divergence handling, and that results are deterministic
Walker 2.7 m/s after fix: is that a sane gait or still an exploit?
questions: What does MuJoCo-on-CPU get on your 4,096-env training wall time end to end versus yours?
Does one thread per robot handle contact count growth, or does this only work for 7 capsules?
Why not Taichi or Genesis on Metal as a baseline?
Is the 40x number on the same float precision and same solver iterations as MuJoCo's?

fixes.change: Lead with end-to-end time-to-policy vs MuJoCo CPU PPO on the same laptop, not raw env-steps/s; show 22x at 4,096 as the headline
Add a small table of existing Mac options (MuJoCo CPU, MJX CPU, Taichi Metal, Genesis) with measured steps/s, so 'no fast path' is evidenced
Replace 'days of practice' headline with wall-clock steps/s or time-to-walk; keep sim-days as a footnote
Show full generated kernel structure (substeps, solver iterations, contact loop) or a profiler trace, not 4 clipped lines
Move CUDA/ROCm portability claim out or label 'not built'; it reads as hand-waving to a CUDA person

first_impression: Unusually honest for a hackathon: reward-hacking story, validation plots, seeds. But validation shows real divergence and rigor is thin.
confusing: Slide 9 title says 'same answers' but the passive-collapse panel shows large trajectory divergence (RMS 0.195 m, 0.562 rad) and open-loop x drifts
Slide 8 numbers: 6.16 m/s on slide vs 'six metres a second' in notes vs 6.64 m/s ablation row; baselines not clearly the same
Slide 7 chart (up to ~60 m, up to 20 s episodes) vs lane replays (21.5 m in 8 s) mixes two metrics
Slide 14 MacGym 21.9 m / MuJoCo 19.8 m vs text 22.0 / 19.7: small inconsistencies
doubts: 'Same answers' overclaims: contact models differ after 0.6-0.8 s, and the headline case (zero-torque collapse) matches worst
Ablation of cheating is single-run; no seeds or confidence intervals on 2.74 vs 6.64 m/s
5 seeds is small, spread is wide (54.9 ± 3.7 m; one seed lags much longer in the chart)
Sim-to-sim to MuJoCo with n=20 and 3/20 falls under mass +20% suggests brittle policy, hand-waved as 'transfers'
Agents wrote most of the code: how much was verified independently versus tests the agents wrote themselves
questions: Which reward terms and observation set did you use, and did PPO hyperparameters change between the cheating and fixed versions?
Is the foot-slip metric validated, or just a threshold chosen after seeing the exploit?
Why do contact models diverge: restitution, friction cone approximation, solver iterations? Did you test convergence with more iterations/substeps?
How would you ablate motor curve and warm-starting jointly with seeds?

fixes.change: Retitle to 'Matches MuJoCo on analytic tests; walker contact diverges after 0.7 s' and show the max-error numbers; honesty beats an overclaim a reviewer will catch
Show the 2x2 ablation (warm-start x motor curve) with speed and slip, multiple seeds and error bars, one consistent baseline number
Plot learning curve with the same metric as lane replays or label both axes in the lane panel; add per-seed time-to-10m
Add the full robustness table with a stated hypothesis for why mass +20% fails (3/20 falls) and a one-line limits box (2D, ground-only, simulated only)
State exactly which parts of validation (tests, MuJoCo comparisons) were written independently of agents
